adversarialFindings.finding: hasWriter is DERIVED, but from a filesystem probe against a WORKING-TREE path, not from merged git state. deriveHasWriter -> writerPathsExist calls existsSync on {engineRoot}/packages/engine-core/scripts/{engineWriterScript}, engineRoot defaulting to a module-anchored sibling '../hauska-engine'. Measured directly: the merged easement writer is on engine origin/main (09e5ea8) but ABSENT from the P:/hauska-engine working tree, which sits on another lane's branch (f1dd938). A refresh run there would have derived hasWriter=false for a writer that IS merged. Worked around by pointing HAUSKA_ENGINE_ROOT at a worktree synced to merged main. D3 removed a process.cwd() dependency; this residual working-tree-REVISION dependency is the same defect class one level up, silent in both directions.

Correctness of the refresh depends on WHERE and on WHICH REVISION the operator runs countyRailRefreshCli. The CLI writes has_writer into county_rail from a local disk probe, and the API serves that stored value (routes/countyLedger.ts:240 reads row.has_writer). A stale or wrong-branch engine checkout silently persists a wrong boolean into the deployment DB, undetectable downstream. Durable fix: derive from the engine's merged git state (a committed writer manifest published by the engine, or git ls-tree origin/main), not from the local working tree.

atomFamilyState is ASSERTED, not derived. It comes from ENGINE_PROPERTY_TYPES_SNAPSHOT, a hand-maintained type list in lib/db/src/schema/enginePropertyTypesSnapshot.ts pinned to engineMainSha "6ccfe8c", many commits behind engine main (09e5ea8). Nothing verifies the pin against live engine state - the hand-declared pattern already recorded for has_writer, still present on the atom-family half.

The CP1 derivation test's fileExists mock is a hardcoded writer allowlist (railManifestDerivation.test.ts). A newly merged writer is invisible to the test until a human adds it, so the suite stays green while asserting a stale world - it asserted 'keeps easement present without writer' at the moment the writer merged. Updated here; the pattern recurs on the next writer merge.

The writer merged with a verify-by-jsonb readback (body->>'atomDid' IN) that no index serves - the form measured at 229,382 ms vs 373 ms per 5,000-id batch at 16.2M+ rows. It passed CI green because no test exercises the readback against a real table. Fixed using easement's own entityId shape (parcelNodeId:easement:easementId, uniform across all three builders), derived from its contract rather than copied from a sibling. Recommend a CI grep banning body->>'atomDid' IN across packages/engine-core/scripts/.

The PR carried CI conclusion "success" while 41 commits behind main and CONFLICTING. A stale-base green is not evidence about the merged result; re-read after rebase (a7f80e1 conclusion string "success"). Worth a branch-freshness gate before treating CI as a merge signal.
